display.purpose: Onboarding and hero moments only — Nunito at its loudest, never for working screens.

headline.purpose: Page and sheet titles, section heroes — Nunito.

title.purpose: Card and list-item titles on the system face; app bars use the Nunito appBarTitle (20).

body.purpose: Reading text; measure stays under 75ch and under the 640 content width on phones.

label.purpose: Buttons, chips, tile labels, captions; overline (10, +1.2 tracking) for eyebrow text.

number.purpose: Dashboard numerals in Nunito 24/34 — the loudest element on any stat tile.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: The default extruded plane — cards, chips, discs, buttons at rest. Both halves always ship together.

shadows.name: pressed
shadows.purpose: A surface mid-press: light and depth swap, the plane sinks. Cards never scale — the lighting change is the signal.

shadows.name: inset
shadows.purpose: Recessed wells — fields, progress tracks, stat icon wells. Always filled, never outlined.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Chrome above other surfaces — nav bar, FAB, dialog, sheet. One offset, cast straight down.

shadows.name: raised-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark mode drops the light source: a faint rim in the surface's own hue plus a near-black depth, slightly tighter.

shadows.name: accent-glow
shadows.purpose: Anchored glow for selected or active elements, parameterised by accent colour. Rationed — the accent may glow, the canvas may not.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Press shadow swaps and the 0.97 scale on buttons and chips (durationFast / durationCard).

motion.name: ease-default
motion.purpose: The default curve for every state change.

motion.name: reduce-motion
motion.purpose: NeuMotion collapses every kit animation to zero duration when the platform asks; state still changes, nothing travels.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Stat grids run two-to-three-up; lists single-column.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one accent action per screen: terracotta fill, umber ink text, pill, extruded pair. Press swaps to the pressed shadows and scales 0.97.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 50px; padding: 0 24px; border: none; border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer; background: #E27D60; color: #2B2118; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.05px; box-shadow: -6px -6px 14px rgba(255,255,255,0.85), 6px 6px 14px rgba(184,174,158,0.55); transition: box-shadow 200ms ease-out, transform 90ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { box-shadow: -8px -8px 18px rgba(255,255,255,0.9), 8px 8px 18px rgba(184,174,158,0.62); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); box-shadow: inset -3px -3px 6px rgba(184,174,158,0.35), inset 3px 3px 6px rgba(255,255,255,0.55); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2B2118; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The quiet sibling: chalk plane, deep terracotta text, same extrusion and press behaviour.

components.description: Brick fill with white text for cancel/delete actions; keeps the pill and the extrusion.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 50px; padding: 0 24px; border: none; border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer; background: #B91C1C; color: #FFFFFF; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.05px; box-shadow: -6px -6px 14px rgba(255,255,255,0.85), 6px 6px 14px rgba(184,174,158,0.55); transition: box-shadow 200ms ease-out, transform 90ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { box-shadow: -8px -8px 18px rgba(255,255,255,0.9), 8px 8px 18px rgba(184,174,158,0.62); } .ds-btn-destructive:active { transform: scale(0.97); box-shadow: inset -3px -3px 6px rgba(184,174,158,0.35), inset 3px 3px 6px rgba(255,255,255,0.55); } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #B91C1C; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: A carved well: recessed bone fill with the inset pair, no border at rest. Focus adds a 2px deep-terracotta ring; a well is never outlined while idle.
components.css: .ds-input { min-width: 260px; padding: 16px 20px; border: none; border-radius: 24px; background: #F1ECE3; color: #111111; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; box-shadow: inset -4px -4px 10px rgba(184,174,158,0.40), inset 4px 4px 10px rgba(255,255,255,0.70); transition: box-shadow 200ms ease-out; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #4A4A4A; opacity: 0.75; } .ds-input:hover { box-shadow: inset -4px -4px 10px rgba(184,174,158,0.46), inset 4px 4px 10px rgba(255,255,255,0.76); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; box-shadow: inset -4px -4px 10px rgba(184,174,158,0.40), inset 4px 4px 10px rgba(255,255,255,0.70), 0 0 0 2px #A8472C; }

components.name: Chip
components.description: Filter/choice pill. Unselected stands proud of the canvas; selected sinks into it with a terracotta-tint wash and deep-terracotta text.
components.css: .ds-chip-row { display: flex; gap: 12px; } .ds-chip { padding: 8px 12px; border: none; border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer; background: #FFFFFF; color: #111111; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1px; box-shadow: -6px -6px 14px rgba(255,255,255,0.85), 6px 6px 14px rgba(184,174,158,0.55); transition: box-shadow 200ms ease-out, background 200ms ease-out, color 200ms ease-out; } .ds-chip:hover { box-shadow: -7px -7px 16px rgba(255,255,255,0.9), 7px 7px 16px rgba(184,174,158,0.6); } .ds-chip--selected, .ds-chip:active { background: #F5E8E0; color: #A8472C; box-shadow: inset -3px -3px 6px rgba(184,174,158,0.35), inset 3px 3px 6px rgba(255,255,255,0.55); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #A8472C; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The workhorse raised plane. Press swaps the pair — the card never scales; the lighting change is the signal at card size.
components.css: .ds-card { width: 280px; padding: 20px; border-radius: 24px; background: #FFFFFF; box-shadow: -6px -6px 14px rgba(255,255,255,0.85), 6px 6px 14px rgba(184,174,158,0.55); transition: box-shadow 200ms ease-out; cursor: pointer; } .ds-card:hover { box-shadow: -8px -8px 18px rgba(255,255,255,0.9), 8px 8px 18px rgba(184,174,158,0.62); } .ds-card:active { box-shadow: inset -3px -3px 6px rgba(184,174,158,0.35), inset 3px 3px 6px rgba(255,255,255,0.55); } .ds-card__title { margin: 0; font-family: 'Nunito', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; color: #111111; } .ds-card__meta { margin: 4px 0 0; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.2px; color: #4A4A4A; }

components.name: Stat Tile
components.description: The clinic pulse unit: icon in a recessed well, the number loudest, the label quietest. Raised, therefore tappable; accent tints appear only on exceptions (waiting > 0, low stock > 0). Unknown values render as a dash, never a fake zero.

narrative.overview:
CarePaw looks like a surface you could press with a fingertip — soft, warm, and continuous. The whole app is one clay plane lit from the top-left: cards stand proud of a warm bone canvas, input wells sink into it, and nothing floats without casting depth. The visual world is built on two layers that must never fight: organic neumorphism owns surfaces, depth, and controls (dual light/depth extrusion on every plane, wells carved into the canvas), while clinic clarity owns layout, type, and colour (warm bone canvas, generous whitespace, exactly one terracotta accent, data-first density).

This system is a deliberate revival, re-executed at full strength. An earlier neumorphic attempt failed on dense clinical screens — edges dissolved, contrast turned to mush. That is treated as a calibration problem, not a direction problem: every shadow value is now a token rather than a per-call-site guess, the depth pair is tinted to the canvas hue instead of left neutral grey, and blur runs at roughly twice the distance so highlights fall off like light rather than like a bevel. Contrast is non-negotiable on top of the effect: accent fills and accent ink are separate tokens, and every text role clears AA in both modes.

The audience is a busy single-clinic operator and pet owners in transit. Screens are phone-first, task-oriented, and read at arm's length at a front desk — so numbers are the loudest element on a dashboard, labels the quietest, and feedback is honest (skeletons, empty states, friendly errors, no silent failures). Motion is budgeted: state changes are shadow swaps and restrained scale, one authored moment per screen, and everything collapses to zero travel when the platform asks for reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Dual extrusion on every plane — a top-left light and a bottom-right tinted depth shadow, always as a pair
Warm bone canvas, terracotta as the only accent, warm charcoal dark mode (never a quick invert)
Nunito for display/headlines/numerals, the system face for body and controls
Token-driven: spacing, radius, depth, and motion come from NeuTokens; colors resolve through ThemeColors
Clay SVG icons as the single icon voice, with Material fallbacks only where the pack has no art
Edges come from shadows, not borders; hairlines appear only where an edge carries data
Reduce-motion is a first-class state: NeuMotion collapses kit animations to zero duration

rules.name: The Text Beats Effect Rule
rules.body: Accent read on the canvas uses Deep Terracotta; accent fills carry Umber Ink; status fills carry white in light mode and ink in dark mode; body text steps down the ink scale, never greys invented per screen.

rules.name: The Tinted Depth Rule
rules.body: Shadows are the canvas hue darkened — Bone Depth (#B8AE9E) and Deep Bone (#7A6E5E) — never neutral grey. A grey shadow on bone reads as dirt.

rules.name: The One Warm Accent Rule
rules.body: Terracotta appears on <=10% of any given screen. Its rarity is what makes it point.

rules.name: The Inherited Colour Rule
rules.body: No AppTextStyles getter bakes in a color. Styles resolve colour from the ambient theme (ColorScheme.onSurface), and call sites that need a specific colour go through ThemeColors / *Of(context) helpers — so a heading is black on light and white on dark with zero per-site branching.

rules.name: The No-Lone-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Never ship one half of the pair on an extruded plane; a single shadow is a sticker, not a surface.

rules.name: The Edge-Carries-Data Rule
rules.body: Hairlines are allowed only where the edge itself is information — separators in data rows, focused fields, table dividers. Decorative borders on cards and wells are banned.

rules.name: The One Step Wider Rule
rules.body: When adding a new surface, take the nearest radius from the radius table — never invent a value, and never go tighter than radiusSm (16) on an extruded plane.

rules.name: The One Icon Voice Rule
rules.body: The user-made clay SVG pack (assets/icons/, rendered by NeuSvgIcon) is the only icon family on shipped surfaces. Multicolor clay art is never tinted with a ColorFilter. Where the pack has no art for a name, ClayIconOrMaterial / optional svgAsset params fall back to Material — a sanctioned exception, not a second style.

dos: Do resolve every colour through ThemeColors (or *Of(context) style helpers) and every gap, radius, and duration through NeuTokens; the tokens are the system.
Do use Deep Terracotta (#A8472C) for accent text/icons on the canvas and Umber Ink (#2B2118) on terracotta fills; verify each new pairing against the Text Beats Effect Rule.
Do pair the light and depth shadows on every extruded plane, with blur >= 2x distance.
Do keep interactive surfaces raised and input surfaces inset; press feedback is the shadow swap (+0.97 scale on buttons/chips only).
Do give every async surface its three honest states: skeleton, empty state with an action, friendly error with retry — never a dead end or a raw exception string.
Do test every screen in both light and dark mode; dark mode drops the light source and leans on the depth shadow.
Do route motion through NeuMotion so reduce-motion collapses it; one authored moment per screen.
donts: Don't use neutral-grey shadows, cool greys in the palette, or white highlights in dark mode — the depth pair is always tinted to the surface's world.
Don't bake a color into a text style, or invent a per-screen grey; step down the ink scale instead.
Don't outline wells, add decorative card borders, or let hairlines appear where no data edge exists.
Don't scale cards on press, animate layouts with bouncy springs, or run more than the budgeted motion.
Don't introduce a second accent, a second icon family, or tinted multicolor clay art.
Don't let the accent exceed its 10% budget, or print fake zeros in place of unknown values.
Don't let the effect win a contrast fight: if a pairing fails AA, the words change the design, not the other way round.
